messages.content: Determine the winner in a Poker game with John having a Hand of 8♥, 10♥, J♥, Q♥, K♥ and Mike having 9♠, J♠, 10♠, Q♠, K♠.

function.name: card_games_poker_determine_winner
function.description: Determines the winner in a game of Poker based on the cards in each players' hands. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

hand1.description: The list of cards (as strings) in first player's hand. E.g ['10♠', 'J♠']

hand2.description: The list of cards (as strings) in second player's hand. E.g ['9♥', '10♥']

message.content:
**Winner:** Mike

**Explanation:**  
Both hands are flushes (all cards of the same suit).  
- John’s flush: 8♥ – 10♥ – J♥ – Q♥ – K♥  
- Mike’s flush: 9♠ – 10♠ – J♠ – Q♠ – K♠  

When comparing flushes, we look at the highest card first, then the next highest, and so on.  
Both have the same highest card (K), the same second (J), third (Q), and fourth (10).  
The deciding card is the fifth: John has 8 while Mike has 9.  
Since 9 > 8, Mike’s flush is higher.  

Therefore, **Mike wins**.
message.reasoning: We need to determine winner. John has 8♥,10♥,J♥,Q♥,K♥. That's a straight flush from 8 to K? Actually 8,10,J,Q,K missing 9. So it's not a straight flush. It's a flush (all hearts). Highest card K. Mike has 9♠,J♠,10♠,Q♠,K♠. That's also a flush (spades). Highest card K. But Mike has 9,10,J,Q,K. John's has 8,10,J,Q,K. So both have same high card K, but next high card J, Q, 10, etc. Compare highest card: both K. Next: J vs J. Next: Q vs Q. Next: 10 vs 10. Next: 8 vs 9. So Mike's 9 beats John's 8. So Mike wins. So answer: Mike wins.
